avatar.reads: an open book — terms somebody looks up, not terms a machine mints

rationale: Owner, 2026-09-23: "put glossary into folio-assistant-core", "it should be part of general pracice w/ glossary/ page", "can glossary be refefences to external skos schema?" (yes), and, on the clash with the harness's own swimlane ledger: "Rename harness one" — so the harness's kind is `swimlane-glossary` and this name belongs here. Registered in code by cat-harness (schemas/glossary-graph-typology.ts) until folio-assistant#2598 (owner, 2026-10-16, "1a"): the harness may not name the layer above it, so the kind is now a node in this layer's typologies/ graph and is named in this layer's namespace, unchanged. Its one family is LISTED with no code: this layer's validator node names it (bean riit). No `validator` path: it resolves under the DECLARING layer's root, and `check:glossary` validates instead. Content, as `scenarios` is: authored or extracted terms and what they mean, true on their own, read by every rendering, written by no process run. The avatar is an OPEN BOOK: a tag or a label would draw the `notation` — one field of a concept, not the thing itself — while a book draws what a reader does with it, looks a word up; tone 84 sits between `qa`'s green verdict and `library`'s, right for a reference rather than a judgement.
description: Terms and what they mean, as W3C SKOS (`folio-glossary/v1`, `schemas/glossary.ts`): local terms, each `authored`, `candidate` or `could-not-extract`, linked to external SKOS concepts by `exactMatch`/`closeMatch`, and external concepts listed as `members` without being copied. A whole external scheme is a `remoteGraphs` entry with `graphTypologies: ["glossary"]`. The `glossary` kind is `perInstance`, so every folio built on this layer gets one. Rendered on the site's `glossary/` page with SKOS JSON-LD beside it; the swimlane ledger is one more source. Read with the [`glossary-terms`](../../library/cataloguing/glossary-terms.md) skill; gated by `check:glossary`.
